A community token built to be checked, not just believed.

StraAIve is a proposed Solana token with a fixed supply of 1,000,000 and a Hope Fund for small, verifiable local projects. Today it is a plan on paper. This site shows the plan and how we intend to prove each step.

1,000,000STRAIVE planned supply

Four commitments behind the proposal

StraAIve starts small on purpose. Each commitment below is a rule the project asks to be held to, not a feature that already exists.

A fixed supply

1,000,000 STRAIVE, no further minting planned and no transfer tax. The on-chain settings get published so anyone can verify them.

A Hope Fund for local projects

15% of supply is set aside for small pilots in food, shelter, education and livelihoods, with public criteria and delivery reports.

Governance that grows in stages

Open discussion first, then test polls, then guarded decisions. No treasury control is handed to a vote until the rules are written down.

Honest status, always

Every page says what exists and what does not. Nothing launches until the readiness checklist is answered in public.

How we intend to work

Six principles from the white paper. They apply to the token, the Hope Fund and the way we talk about both.

Dignity

Help should respect people. Hardship is never a marketing tool.

Transparency

Allocations, treasury moves, votes and impact claims are documented in public.

Accessibility

Plain-language learning material. Nobody has to buy a token to take part or to ask for help.

Accountability

We publish what was planned, what was spent and what can be verified.

Security before speed

Test, review and document critical systems before they hold meaningful value.

Honest communication

Proposals are labeled as proposals. Aspirations are never presented as results.

One supply, seven purposes

The proposed split of 1,000,000 STRAIVE. Hover a row or a segment to see how it fits. An allocation is a plan for stewardship, not tokens already in circulation.

A fixed supply limits how many tokens exist. It says nothing about price. STRAIVE could be volatile, hard to trade, or worth little or nothing. Contributor tokens are proposed to vest over a 12-month cliff plus 36 months, which is a plan and not yet an implemented lockup.

150,000 tokens is not 150,000 dollars.

The Hope Fund can only help as much as its real, realizable resources allow. So it starts with small pilots, and reports what was received, what was delivered and what can honestly be credited to the project.

Food securityMeal programs and essential supplies through accountable local partners.
Shelter and basic needsSmall initiatives that improve access to safe shelter and essential services.
Education and skillsLearning materials, training and scholarships where delivery can be verified.
LivelihoodsPractical, income-generating skills and community resilience projects.

How the Fund should operate

  • Publish criteria. What qualifies, what evidence is needed, how proposals are scored and how conflicts are handled.
  • Start small. Limited pilots with measurable outputs before any expansion.
  • Track every conversion. When tokens are sold, swapped or donated, disclose amounts, dates, fees and use of proceeds.
  • Protect beneficiaries. No sensitive personal data published. Nobody has to buy or hold STRAIVE to receive help.
  • Report honestly. Separate committed, received, delivered and attributable outcomes.
  • Show the evidence. A Proof of Impact record: receipts, partner confirmations, anonymized delivery records and feedback.

A staged roadmap, with proof at each step

No dates yet. We add them only when resources, owners and dependencies are understood. Every phase is planned and none is complete.

  1. 1

    Foundation Planned

    Confirm the token design, publish documentation and risk disclosures, and open feedback channels.

    Done when: parameters, an issue list and a decisions log are public.

  2. 2

    Testnet Planned

    Create the token and test basic distribution flows on Solana testnet.

    Done when: testnet addresses, reproducible test steps and known limitations are published.

  3. 3

    Governance and treasury design Planned

    Draft proposal rules, treasury safeguards, vesting details and Hope Fund selection criteria.

    Done when: policies and the community review record are published.

  4. 4

    Pilot impact projects Planned

    Select one small, verifiable community pilot with accountable delivery partners.

    Done when: criteria, the decision record, delivery evidence and a public report exist.

  5. 5

    Security and launch decision Planned

    Complete technical checks, independent review where feasible and a legal and regulatory assessment.

    Done when: review findings are public and an explicit go or no-go is recorded.

  6. 6

    Mainnet and iteration Planned

    Consider launch only after readiness requirements are met, then improve from evidence.

    Done when: the live configuration, wallet disclosures and operating procedures are verified and reported.

Governance, one careful stage at a time

Participation should be meaningful without putting the treasury or participants at avoidable risk.

Open discussion

Proposals are published, feedback is invited and questions get public answers.

Non-binding testnet polls

Voting tools are tested with no real treasury assets at risk.

Guarded decisions

Binding votes start only after eligibility, quorum, conflict and emergency rules are documented.

Periodic review

Activity and status are published, including the reason when a decision can't be carried out.

Safeguards we plan to write into the rules

Holding tokens does not guarantee influence unless the adopted voting rules say so.

Rules address concentrated voting power, duplicate participation, proposal spam and conflicts of interest.

Treasury actions need multi-party controls and public records where possible.

A vote cannot override the law, safety requirements or the duty to protect personal data.

No DAO, binding voting system or on-chain treasury process exists today.

Before any launch, we answer yes to all of these

  • Token parameters, supply, decimals, authorities and program are verified and documented.
  • Allocation wallets and transfer rules are published, with no unexplained wallets.
  • Contributor vesting terms are final, disclosed and enforceable where feasible.
  • Treasury access uses documented controls, including multi-party approval.
  • The liquidity policy explains permitted actions, risks, custody and reporting.
  • Hope Fund eligibility, decision process and beneficiary safeguards are public.
  • Governance rules cover proposals, voting, quorum, conflicts and emergencies.
  • Testnet testing is documented and known limits are disclosed.
  • Independent security review and legal review have been pursued, and findings addressed or disclosed.
  • Every public message separates what exists from what is only an idea.

Risks, stated plainly

Market and liquidity

STRAIVE may be volatile, hard to trade, or worth little or nothing. Providing liquidity can lose value and does not guarantee price stability.

Technical

Contract or configuration errors, compromised keys and software defects can cause lost assets. Testnet use and reviews reduce some risks but can't remove them.

Governance and concentration

Voting power or treasury access may become concentrated, and proposals can be manipulated or poorly executed.

Impact delivery

A token allocation is not a cash reserve. What the Hope Fund can deliver depends on realizable resources, trustworthy partners and operating capacity.

Legal and regulatory

Rules on crypto-assets, fundraising, tax and consumer protection vary by country and change. Qualified legal and accounting advice is required before launch or public distribution.

No guarantee

Nothing here guarantees profit, token value, exchange listings, grants or any governance outcome. Participation is voluntary and carries risk.

Allocation
A planned assignment of tokens to a purpose. Not necessarily distributed or liquid.
Vesting
A schedule that limits when allocated tokens become available to a recipient.
Mint authority
The permission that can create new tokens. We intend to revoke it after the first mint.
Testnet
A practice network for experiments, not for ordinary use with real value.
